revocation.how: This manifest is the source of truth. A revoked key has status:'revoked' and a valid_to timestamp; proofs whose created_at falls after valid_to are no longer trusted.

how_to_check_freshness: Confirm a proof's verifier_pubkey matches an entry in `keys` whose window (valid_from..valid_to) contains the proof's created_at, and that the entry is not status:'revoked'. Then recompute the signature offline.
verify_offline: npm i invinoveritas-verify  ·  pip install invinoveritas-verify

pq_key_binding.note: Post-quantum readiness: an anchored, dual-signed (Schnorr + ML-DSA-65) statement binding this key to a real PQ key, so a future quantum forger who derives the secp256k1 key alone cannot mint a valid PQ-bound identity. This pointer is discovery only — the linked artifact is content-addressed and self-verifying (recompute + check both signatures + the Bitcoin OTS anchor); do not trust this manifest as authority for the binding itself.

manifest_anchor_history.note: This manifest's own trust-relevant state (verifier_pubkey/keys/revocation) is periodically Bitcoin-OTS-anchored, so a key rotation or a history edit is checkable against a real timeline, not just this response's current claim. Discovery only — recompute the state hash yourself and verify the .ots proof before trusting any entry there.
